title: SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot: structured document generation with Forms
summary: The briefing's rollout, licensing, permissions and documented limitations are supported by the roadmap, Microsoft's notice and Microsoft Learn. No blocking errors were found; minor corrections concern the action rating and a licensing check missing from the controls table.

claims.claim: Only Microsoft Word documents in .docx format can be used as source templates.
claims.quote: Supported file types — Only Microsoft Word documents (.docx) support creating templates.

claims.claim: Structured document generation turns Word templates in a SharePoint document library into forms.
claims.quote: You can create a form from any Word document stored in a SharePoint document library.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Submitting the form generates a new document with the submitted values merged into the template fields.
claims.quote: When a user submits a form, the system automatically generates a new document from the template with the submitted values merged into the appropriate fields.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes a content manager who creates and governs templates and forms.
claims.quote: Content manager (template creator) - Creates and governs templates and forms.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes a content consumer who fills out a form to generate a document.
claims.quote: Content consumer (form submitter) - Submits forms to generate documents. They fill out the form with the requested information, and the system generates a new document

claims.claim: Form creation begins with Forms in the library command bar, then Document generation form, followed by uploading a Word template.
claims.quote: In a SharePoint document library, select Forms from the command bar. ... Select Document generation form to start the form creation process. ... Upload the Word document you want to use as a template.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Copilot in SharePoint analyses the uploaded document and suggests fields such as names, dates and addresses.
claims.quote: Copilot in SharePoint analyzes the structure of the document and automatically suggests fields—such as names, dates, addresses, and responsibilities

claims.claim: The creator reviews the suggested fields.
claims.quote: Review the suggested fields. You can: ... Confirm which fields are required. ... Refine field names to match your organization's terminology.

claims.claim: The creator can set field data types.
claims.quote: Type — Select the data type for the field from the Type dropdown.

claims.claim: Creators can define conditional sections in the document template.
claims.quote: Conditional sections let you control which parts of the generated document are included based on the values that form submitters enter.

claims.claim: Generated file output can be Word (.docx) or PDF.
claims.quote: Select file type — Choose the format for the generated document: Word (.docx) or PDF (.pdf).

claims.claim: Creators can configure a file name pattern.
claims.quote: Set file name pattern — Define how generated files are named by combining fields and text

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Form submitters need only the form link, not access to the destination document library.
claims.quote: Form submitters need only the form link (Read access to the template is granted automatically). ... You don't need access to the destination document library to submit the form.

claims.claim: Form submitters receive Read access to the template automatically.
claims.quote: Read access to the template is granted automatically

claims.claim: Form submitters do not automatically receive access to the destination document library.
claims.quote: Form submitters don't automatically receive access to the destination document library.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Viewing a generated document requires a separate access grant or the form creator's receipt option.
claims.quote: You must grant access to view the generated document separately, or the form creator can enable the receipt option.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: PDF generation does not work if sensitivity labels are enabled for the site or library, with support described as coming soon.
claims.quote: PDF generation doesn't work if sensitivity labels are enabled for the site or library. Support for that feature is coming soon.

claims.claim: Conditional sections do not update after changing a field value in a generated document opened in Word for the web.
claims.quote: In a generated document opened in Word for the web, conditional sections don't update when you change a field value after generation—the hidden and shown sections stay as they were at generation time.

claims.claim: Form submitted (Preview) triggers a Power Automate flow when a form is submitted.
claims.quote: Form submitted (Preview) triggers a flow when a form is submitted, so you can start workflows such as approvals or notifications.

claims.claim: Get form metadata (Preview) is one of the feature's Power Automate capabilities.
claims.quote: Get form metadata (Preview) retrieves the form structure, so you can map responses to fields without manual configuration.

claims.claim: Generate document from form (Preview) lets a Power Automate flow generate and save documents without the form UI.
claims.quote: Generate document from form (Preview) creates documents by mapping input data to a document generation template and saves the output to a SharePoint library.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn page describes no autonomous generation, distinct from the explicitly acknowledged Power Automate workflows.
claims.quote: Searched: "structured document generation" "processing" "autonomous". Read the entire structured-document-generation page, including Fill out and submit a form and Use Power Automate; it describes submissions and configured flows, not autonomous agent decisions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Power Automate does not apply conditional field visibility, so fields hidden in a form can appear in flow-generated documents.
claims.quote: Power Automate doesn't apply conditional visibility: if you generate documents through a Power Automate flow, the flow doesn't hide or show fields the way the form does, so a required field that your form hides will still be visible in the document.

claims.claim: Published form fields are read-only in SharePoint for structural changes, which require editing the Word template and republishing.
claims.quote: After you publish a form, the form fields are read-only in the SharePoint form view. To make structural changes to fields, edit the template in Word.

claims.claim: The form link remains the same after updating and republishing the template.
claims.quote: The form link is persistent—it stays the same URL even when you update and republish the template.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature's Learn page states no meter, credit rate or price for structured document generation.
claims.quote: Searched: "structured document generation" "Copilot Credits" licensing billing. Read the complete feature page, Copilot in SharePoint get-started and the Copilot Credits billing overview; the feature page names no meter, rate or price.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature's Learn page lists no licence requirement or extra charge for form submitters.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint structured document generation forms disable admin control PowerShell Graph licensing Copilot Credits billing. Read the feature page's Prerequisites and Requirements and limitations; licensing is specified for creators, not submitters.

claims.claim: The separate Copilot in SharePoint page says advanced work requires usage-based billing and consumes Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Advanced work requires usage-based billing and consumes Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The reviewed documentation does not explicitly classify structured document generation as advanced work or state its Copilot Credits treatment.
claims.quote: Searched: "structured document generation" "Copilot Credits" licensing billing. Opened the feature page, Copilot in SharePoint get-started and Copilot Credits billing overview; none explicitly places form-driven template generation in the advanced-work billing class.

claims.claim: Beyond analysing the template to suggest fields, the feature page gives no further account of Copilot processing the template.
claims.quote: Searched: "structured document generation" "processing" "autonomous". Read the full feature page, including Create a form from a document and Detect potential fields; no further Copilot template-processing mechanism is described.

claims.claim: Copilot in SharePoint has a Site AI settings panel for site owners.
claims.quote: The Site AI settings panel lets site owners manage how users interact with AI on their site, including Copilot in SharePoint.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is an availability control respected by Copilot in SharePoint generally.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing setting that's respected. If it's enabled on a site, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions don't appear on that site.

claims.claim: The reviewed documentation does not confirm that Site AI settings or Restricted Content Discovery govern structured document generation forms.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint structured document generation Forms Site AI Restricted Content Discovery Microsoft Forms turn off applies. Read feature and get-started pages and Restricted Content Discovery excerpts; none explicitly places these forms under those AI entry-point controls.

claims.claim: The Copilot in SharePoint page says preview PowerShell availability controls are being retired.
claims.quote: Copilot in SharePoint is retiring the PowerShell commands used to opt tenants and sites in or out during preview

claims.claim: Microsoft Forms has documented controls to turn it off or on for an organisation or specific people.
claims.quote: If you're an admin, you can set up Microsoft Forms, then turn it off or turn it on again for your entire organization or just specific people.

claims.claim: The reviewed documentation does not confirm whether the Microsoft Forms on/off setting governs document-generation forms created in SharePoint libraries.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint structured document generation Forms Site AI Restricted Content Discovery Microsoft Forms turn off applies. Opened Forms on/off and structured-generation feature pages; neither states this setting's applicability to these library forms.

claims.claim: The feature page publishes no price for template administration time or generated-document storage.
claims.quote: Searched: "structured document generation" "Copilot Credits" licensing billing. Read the entire feature page; it describes template configuration and library storage but publishes no price for either.

claims.claim: Submitters automatically see updated fields after the template is republished.
claims.quote: Form submitters automatically see the updated fields after republishing.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Published-form document generation is available based on standard SharePoint permissions.
claims.quote: Document generation through published forms will be available based on standard SharePoint permissions.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to check Copilot licence assignments is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: "Confirm which users hold a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence". The only controls row is "A switch specific to structured document generation"; it is not a licence-assignment control.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet beginning 'Confirm which users hold a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence'. It names a licensing control with no table row; retain the verified licence prerequisite in Cost and licensing and Scope.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits the standard for this launched, on-by-default feature with medium risk and cost and a governance decision to take.
claims.quote: Fields: status "launched", defaultState "on", risk "medium", cost "medium", action "prepare". Governance advice: "agree who may create templates". The standard assigns act-now to launched automatic changes with medium risk or cost and a decision to take.
claims.fix: Change front matter action from 'prepare' to 'act-now': as of 17 November 2026 the feature is launched, on by default, and the briefing identifies an outstanding template-ownership decision.

claims.claim: Microsoft identifies contracts, agreements and offer letters as uses for structured document generation.
claims.quote: Legal and compliance - Contracts, NDAs, statements of work, settlement agreements, vendor agreements. ... Human resources - Employment verification letters, offer letters, travel and visa support letters.

claims.claim: The Learn page describes sharing the form link with users in the organisation.
claims.quote: After you publish the form, share the form link so users in your organization can submit forms and generate documents.
